title: Similar triangles: measuring a tree with its shadow
examples: How can you measure a tree with its shadow?
How do you find a missing side in similar shapes?

items.label: Tree 8 m
items.ask: How do you find a missing side in similar shapes?

explain.say: How tall is a tree? You cannot climb it with a tape measure. But on a sunny day, shadows can tell you! Look at the four bars: a stick, its shadow, the tree's shadow, and the tree.

draw.text: Similar triangles: measuring a tree with its shadow

items.label: Tree 8 m
items.ask: How do you find a missing side in similar shapes?

explain.say: Stand a 1 metre stick in the ground. Its shadow is 2 metres long. So the shadow is 2 times the height. Look at the stick shadow bar.

items.label: Tree 8 m
items.ask: How do you find a missing side in similar shapes?

explain.say: At the same moment, the tree's shadow is 16 metres. The sun hits both at the same angle, so they make similar triangles: the same shape, but different sizes. What do you think the tree's height is?

items.label: Tree 8 m
items.ask: How do you find a missing side in similar shapes?

explain.say: The shadow is always 2 times the height. So the tree is 16 divided by 2: 8 metres tall! Similar shapes keep the same ratio between their sides.

items.label: Tree 8 m
items.ask: How do you find a missing side in similar shapes?

explain.say: Wonderful! A famous story says the Greek thinker Thales measured an Egyptian pyramid this way. Challenge: a 1.5 metre person casts a 3 metre shadow. A building casts a 30 metre shadow. How tall is the building?

because.label: Same sun angle
because.note: Light hits the stick and tree at the same angle
because.ask: Why are the two triangles similar?

because.label: Same angles
because.note: Both triangles have the same three angles

because.label: Same ratio
because.note: Shadow is 2 times the height for both

faq.a: Similar shapes have the same shape but different sizes. Their angles are equal, and their sides are in the same ratio.
asks: What does similar mean in maths?

faq.q: Why are the two triangles similar?
faq.a: The stick and the tree both stand straight up, and the sun's rays hit them at the same angle. So both triangles have the same angles.
asks: Why do shadows make similar triangles?

faq.q: How do you find a missing side in similar shapes?
faq.a: Find the scale factor or the ratio from a pair of matching sides, then use it. The shadow is 2 times the height, so a 16 metre shadow means an 8 metre tree.

faq.q: What is the difference between similar and congruent?
faq.a: Congruent shapes are exactly the same size and shape. Similar shapes are the same shape, but one can be bigger.

faq.q: How did Thales measure a pyramid?
faq.a: The story says he waited until his shadow was as long as he was tall. At that moment the pyramid's shadow was also as long as its height.

facts: In similar triangles, corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
Thales of Miletus, who lived around 600 BCE, is said to have measured the height of a pyramid using shadows.

quiz.say: A 2 metre pole casts a 3 metre shadow. A tower casts a 30 metre shadow at the same time. How tall is the tower?
quiz.show: Pole 2 m, shadow 3 m. Tower shadow 30 m
quiz.why: The tower shadow is 10 times the pole shadow, so the tower is 10 times 2, which is 20 metres.

wrong.1: 45 uses the ratio the wrong way round.

quiz.say: Two triangles are similar. What must be true?
quiz.why: Similar shapes have equal angles; their sides are in the same ratio.

wrong.1: Equal sides would make them congruent.
wrong.2: Areas are equal only if they are the same size.
